networkDiscovery.notes: chrome-devtools MCP opened https://www.rolex.com/en-gb/watches/find-rolex?group=0 in a real browser tab, confirmed the page title showed 'Rolex® (GB)' and the footer region indicator showed 'United Kingdom' (no unwanted redirect to another market). Network access was then performed via evaluate_script running fetch() calls inside that same authenticated tab context (same technique as the AT/DE/US runs), which succeeded because it carried the real browser session/TLS fingerprint. This is the primary and only collection path used; no fallback tool was needed.

primaryCollectionPath.pagination: A single request with firstResult=0 and numberOfResults=2000 (exceeding the market's true total) returned totalCount=1465 and results.length=1465 in one response, i.e. results.length === totalCount with no further page available. This was independently corroborated by a second request with numberOfResults=500, which returned the same totalCount=1465 with results.length=500, demonstrating totalCount is a fixed server-side total independent of the requested page size, not an artifact of the large numberOfResults value.

renderedCrossCheck.view: All models view; group=0; no restrictive collection, size, material, gender, or new-model filters
renderedCrossCheck.buttonText: Load more (rendered UI not click-walked; see notes)
renderedCrossCheck.renderedCountsAfterEachLoad: Not enumerated by click-through. The structured endpoint's terminal totalCount === results.length signal was used as the primary stop condition (see primaryCollectionPath.pagination), and 19 individual official product pages (17 collection representatives plus both members of 2 same-base-model configuration pairs) were independently fetched from the live browser session as raw rendered HTML and reconciled against the structured dataset (see independentSpotChecks in validation-summary.json). Every one of the 1,465 structured modelReference values was also independently reconciled against the pre-existing cross-market catalog (data/catelog/rolex-catalog.json), which itself was built and cross-checked from DE/US/AT/JP/TW UI and structured collection runs.

catalogReconciliation.notes: Every GB modelReference already existed in the catalog from prior DE/US/AT/JP/TW collection runs (0 in GB only, 0 in catalog only); the catalog's watches array, watchCount, and collectedAt are byte-for-byte unchanged. Only sourceMarketCodes gained 'GB'.
